diego: hi all, first day here on infra team. quick mapping q: who owns SLOs/alert thresholds for hosted vs dedicated customers, and who to ask for quota/billing increases for a Dedicated pool?

viv: welcome! :wave: SLO ownership: eng-platform owns product-facing SLOs for model serving (latency, error-rate) across hosted/dedicated. eng-sre monitors infra-level SLOs (node health, kube control plane).

sam: for alerts, platform teams set service-level alerts; eng-sre owns node/cluster alerts. If you're unsure which alert fired, ping both teams and tag @viv.

diego: who approves quota bumps for Dedicated capacity (more GPUs) and billing questions?

kait: billing/quota flow: capacity requests -> sales/account exec initiates quote -> finance approves charges -> infra schedules capacity. For internal dev quotas, infra can grant short-term increases. For customer-facing Dedicated commits, loop in sales and finance early.

finance-bot: Note: Budget approvals for Dedicated must include account code and annual commit. Contacts: @kait (finance), @sales-lead (account exec).

diego: ok. and PagerDuty for dedicated infra vs hosted infra? same on-call teams?

oncall-bot: Hosted API incidents -> eng-platform on-call. Dedicated customer infra -> eng-sre on-call; eng-runtime if runtime-level. See on-call calendar: https://redwood.internal/oncall-calendar

sam: extra nuance: if a Dedicated customer reports a latency SLA miss, tag eng-platform first and CC the account exec. For hardware failures in a Dedicated pool page eng-sre.

diego: where's the single source of truth for owner/contact per component?

viv: handbook has ownership matrix: https://redwood.internal/handbook/ownership-matrix. We also keep a short owners list in the runbooks under /runbooks/owners. If you don't have access, hit #help and @sam will add you.

diego: great, thanks — I'll file access and loop my manager for approvals. excited to be here! :tada:
